name: Rails CSRF Protection Disabled
attack_scenario: Attacker hosts a page that auto-submits a POST to /account/email; the victim's session cookie rides along and, with CSRF checks off, the email (and account recovery) is changed silently.
negative_test_hint: submit a cross-origin POST to "/account/email" carrying the session cookie but no CSRF token and assert the request is rejected with 403 rather than applied

exemplar.explanation: Skipping verify_authenticity_token (or skip_forgery_protection) turns off Rails CSRF token checking for state-changing actions, so any origin can forge authenticated requests. Keep protect_from_forgery with: :exception; for token-authenticated APIs, authenticate by bearer token rather than disabling the check on session-cookie routes.
